intro:
Zborov

July 2nd, 1917

Four months ago there was a Tsar. There is now a Provisional Government, a committee in every regiment, and an offensive ordered by a minister who has never commanded anything.

Half the divisions here have voted not to attack, and the men are not cowards: they have worked out that the government asking for one more push is the same one that will not give them the land. The Czechoslovak brigade is the exception - seven thousand men for whom capture means a rope. Their objective is Pluhiv, behind the Austrian third line.

briliant.text:
Pluhiv is taken, and with it three lines of trenches, sixty-two officers, more than three thousand men and fifteen guns, for a loss of about two hundred killed. The volunteers went through a position that a rifle corps on our right refused to leave its own trenches to look at.

It changes nothing about the offensive, which will be over in a fortnight and will end with our army retreating past Tarnopol. It changes a great deal about the brigade: Kerensky will let them recruit from the prisoner camps and they will be a corps by the winter.

It changed something in me as well, though I could not have said what on the day. I have watched Czech conscripts come across no-man's-land with their hands up to men they recognised, and I have watched a Russian division stand in its trench and vote. Those are the same fact seen twice. An army does not fight for a government it has stopped believing in, and this government has four months left.

We took the first line and were held in the second. The brigade lost a fifth of its strength for a field and a wood, and the corps on our flank never moved at all.

The offensive is finished before it started. We will go over the same ground again when the orders are rewritten.

intro:
Kiev

February 28th, 1918

The old army has not weakened, it has dissolved: there are no armies, there are trains full of men going home. Eleven German divisions are marching into the Ukraine at forty versts a day.

In Kiev is everything Soviet power in the Ukraine still owns - the arsenal detachments, the Red Guard, the archives, the treasury, and eleven thousand people who will be shot or hanged if they are here when the Germans arrive. Five days: hold the Dnieper bridges until they are out.

briliant.text:
Five days, and the bridges were still standing when the last of the column was over them. Then we blew them.

Kiev is German. The Rada rode in behind them and will be dismissed by them in April, at gunpoint, in favour of a Hetman who wants the estates back - which is how a national government becomes an occupation's clerk in eight weeks.

The regiment that held the bridges with us broke contact cleanly and rejoined its corps. We shook hands at Darnitsa. They are going to Vladivostok, they say, and then to France, and they want nothing to do with our civil war.

I believed them at the time.

The northern bridge was rushed on the fourth day and the crossing was under machine-gun fire before the column was half over. What was still on the western bank stayed there.

The arsenal detachments are gone, the archives are gone, and the people we were holding the bridges for are in German hands. We are going east with what walked out.

intro:
Bachmach

March 13th, 1918

The treaty signed on the third is the worst peace any Russian government has put its name to - Poland, the Baltic, Finland, the Ukraine, a third of the population. A government with no army cannot bargain.

The new border is east of here, and through this junction must pass sixty thousand legionnaires and every train of grain that can be got out. The Legion covers the junction, we cover the crossing, by written agreement - the last of its kind. Hold Konotop and Bachmach until the echelons are through.

briliant.text:
The junction held for the four days the timetable needed and the German advance was stopped dead in front of it - which is a sentence very few people wrote in the spring of 1918.

The echelons are through. Theirs and ours, on the same line, with the same signals, under the same guns.

The Legion goes east now under an agreement with Moscow: free passage to Vladivostok along the Trans-Siberian, one company's worth of rifles per echelon and the rest of the arms handed in. Sixty thousand men strung out over six thousand versts of railway in a country with no government worth the name and a great many people who would like sixty thousand rifles.

I wrote in my report that the arrangement was sound provided nobody on either side lost his head. I would like that sentence back.

We lost the grain trains and four echelons of our own. The Legion got its people out; we did not get all of ours.

intro:
Chelyabinsk

May 14th, 1918

It began with a stove leg thrown from a train. Legionnaires going east, Hungarian and Austrian prisoners going home under the treaty, and four years of a war they were all in on opposite sides between them.

The Soviet arrested the men who lynched the thrower, which was correct; the Legion took the arsenal and freed them by force, which was not; and Moscow has wired an order to disarm a corps strung out over six thousand versts, which it will refuse. Hold the Chelyabinsk prison and the station.

briliant.text:
The prison and the eastern stations held. The Soviet's people, the Party committee and about four hundred railway workers with their families went out on the last trains east; the internationalist company covered the platform to the end and about half of it is still with us.

The town is theirs. By the end of the month so are Penza, Novonikolayevsk, Tomsk and Omsk - not because the Legion is strong but because every officers' union and every Committee of the Constituent Assembly in Siberia has been waiting three months for exactly this, and now has a corps to hide behind.

The Eastern Front is being formed today by decree. Everything we do for the next year starts from this station.

Chelyabinsk is gone, the Urals line is cut, and there is nothing organised between here and the Volga.

intro:
Samara

May 26th, 1918

The Committee of the Constituent Assembly has declared itself the government of Russia in a building whose garrison it has not taken. Five deputies, a press, and an understanding with the Legion's echelons.

This is the shape of the whole summer: foreign troops who say they only want to go home take the towns, and the government behind them will be swept away by Kolchak's officers in November. Hold Samara and the stations long enough to get the Party organisation, the treasury and the arms over the bridge.

briliant.text:
The city held to the hour and the evacuation went out over the bridge: the committee, the treasury, four hundred rifles and the workers who could not stay.

Samara falls in the second week of June. Its Soviet will not be in it when it does, and the men who would have been shot in the yard behind the station are at Simbirsk forming into a regiment.

The Committee's government lasts four months. Long enough to raise a People's Army by conscription, discover that conscripted peasants will not fight for it, and be arrested by the officers it invited to protect it.

Samara is the Committee's capital, the Volga is their river as far as Simbirsk, and the gold reserve at Kazan is now four days' march from a front that does not exist.

intro:
Kazan

August 7th, 1918

Six hundred million roubles of Imperial gold are in the vaults under this city, still here because the order to move them came too late. That is why the attack is here and not somewhere sensible.

Kappel has three thousand men; the Fifth Army is nine days old and includes a Latvian regiment whose commander goes over to them tomorrow. Nobody is promised the gold stays. What can be saved is the army and the crossings - and an army that exists in August can come back for Kazan in September.

briliant.text:
The city held to the last hour and the Fifth Army came out over the Volga as an army, with its guns, and with about a hundred tons of the reserve on the barges.

The rest is theirs. Eight train-loads of it went east within the week and it will follow Kolchak to Omsk, to Irkutsk, and eventually into the hands of the Legion, who will trade it - and him - to us for a free passage in January 1920.

Trotsky's train is at Sviyazhsk. What arrives with it is a field tribunal, a printing press, commissars for every regiment and reinforcements from Moscow, and within four weeks the Fifth Army is a different thing entirely.

The Kremlin fell with the vaults under it and the crossing went the same afternoon. The Fifth Army is on the western bank in fragments.

They have the whole reserve and we have nothing on the Volga above Nizhny. This is their high-water mark and it did not have to be this high.

intro:
Omsk

December 22nd, 1918

On the eighteenth of November the officers arrested the Directory in its beds, and Admiral Kolchak has proclaimed himself Supreme Ruler in Omsk, with British advisers and Japanese money.

Tonight the city rises: the Kulomzino workshops, the garrison's Second Regiment, the underground, and two hundred prisoners who will be freed or shot depending on the hour. It will be put down, and the five hundred shot for it will teach every village in Siberia to hate this government. Hold the workers' quarters long enough for those who can get out to get out.

briliant.text:
The quarters held into the second night, which was all that was ever going to be possible, and the people who could walk went out over the ice.

The rising is over. The reprisals are not: they will go on for a week, and the amnesty the garrison offered on the second day will be honoured by nobody. Some of those who came out with us are with the Kulomzino men in the forest tonight and will be a partisan regiment by the spring.

That is the arithmetic of this whole regime, and it is why it will not last two years. It cannot hold a city without shooting the people in it, and every man it shoots recruits four for the taiga.

intro:
Semenov

February 10th, 1920

Kolchak was shot at Irkutsk three days ago by sentence of a revolutionary committee, after the Legion handed him over with the gold for a clear line east.

What is left is Transbaikalia, which was never really his. Ataman Semenov has held the line from Chita eastward for two years on Japanese money and armoured trains, station by station, with a firing party. The partisans here are the villages themselves and have fought him without us since 1918. Chita is the knot.

briliant.text:
Chita is taken and the ataman is on a train east with what he could carry.

He will spend the twenties in Japan and Manchuria, on somebody's payroll, and will be hanged in Moscow in 1946, which is longer than most of the people he hanged got.

The partisan detachments are being formed into regiments of the People's Revolutionary Army - the Far Eastern Republic's, not ours, on paper, because there are Japanese divisions in Vladivostok and Moscow has decided not to give them a reason to stay. A buffer state with a parliament and a flag, which will vote itself into the Republic the moment the last Japanese transport clears the harbour.

The ataman keeps the line for another season, and everything east of Baikal with it.

intro:
Vladivostok

March 10th, 1920

Nine thousand versts of railway from Bachmach, and a city at the end of it that belongs to nobody in particular. In January the partisans and the Zemstvo took Vladivostok without much of a fight.

What they did not take, and cannot, is the garrison: Japanese divisions in the port and the last of the Legion on the quay. Tokyo has not decided whether to go or to stay; in three weeks it will decide to stay. Nobody takes this city in March 1920 - bring the couriers through to the contact point.

briliant.text:
The contact was made. Our people are in the city, the lists went with them, and the organisation that will run this coast for the next two years now exists on paper as well as in somebody's memory.

On the quay I found the 2nd Regiment - the one that held the Kiev bridges with us in 1918 - waiting for a ship. Two years of a war they did not want, in a country they were only trying to cross, and they are going home to a republic that exists now, which is what they set out for at Zborov. We did not shake hands. There was too much between the bridges at Kiev and the gaol yard at Chelyabinsk for that.

The Japanese leave in 1922 and the buffer state votes itself into the Republic a fortnight later. That is the last of the intervention and the last of the war.

As for me: I went into 1917 as a captain of the old army seconded to somebody else's brigade, and I come out of 1920 as a commander of the Red Army with nothing in common with the man who marched on Pluhiv except the memory. I was never a legionary. I was a Russian officer who worked out, in a trench in Galicia while a division voted, which side of his own country he was on. The campaign is over.

intro:
Kazan: the Red offensive

September 10th, 1918

One month, and the Fifth Army has been rebuilt from the outside in: commissars, tribunals, a supply service, forty-eight guns, the Volga flotilla brought up from Nizhny.

Opposite, the People's Army is coming apart - conscripts deserting in companies, the Legion going home after all, and Kappel's three thousand unable to hold a city of two hundred thousand that does not want them. This is the first attack this army has made. Take the Romanov Bridge, Kazan and the eastern railway.

briliant.text:
Kazan is ours. The bridge was taken intact by a battalion that crossed in the dark on barges, the city fell in a day and a half, and their column went east along the railway with the flotilla shelling the embankment.

Simbirsk follows in two days - Tukhachevsky's 1st Army took it and wired Lenin about it while he was still in bed with a bullet in him. Syzran and Samara before the snow.

The turn on this front happened here, and it happened because an army that was beaten in August was not destroyed in August. That is worth remembering the next time somebody is told to hold a crossing for four more days.

intro:
Ufa

June 9th, 1919

Ufa was taken this morning: the Fifth Army crossed the Belaya on rafts in the dark with Chapayev's division leading, and the Siberian Army is going back over the Urals with our cavalry in its transport.

Kolchak's spring offensive collapsed for reasons that had nothing to do with the fighting. He mobilised the villages and they deserted, restored the landlords and the villages rose, let his atamans hang people along the railway and the railway stopped working. Take Alatorka and the Iglino junction east of the city.

briliant.text:
The junctions are ours and about forty echelons with them - guns, British rifles still in their grease, four hospital trains and a printing works.

The pursuit goes on to Chelyabinsk in July and Omsk in November, and it is the villages that make it possible: they cut the line behind him faster than we can advance on it.

The Legion is not fighting us here. It has been pulled back to guard the Trans-Siberian, it wants nothing except a ship at Vladivostok, and by the autumn its commanders will be sending open letters to Paris about what is being done in the country they are policing. A year late, but they will send them.
